Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Time, the calendar & feasts

yesterday adverb and noun

also yesterday’s

classical

Cic. Fam. 11.1.1: heri vesperī (Lewis & Short)
Sen. Ep. 64.1: fuistī here nōbīscum
Traupman 89

heri (here)

adverb

Lewis & Short: heri is perhaps the only form in Cicero; here is the usual one after the Augustan age (Quint. 1.7.22).

Other words

  • hesternus, hesterna, hesternum — yesterday’s, of yesterday

    adjective · also used · classical · Catull. 50.1: hesternō … diē; Ov. Fast. 5.506: ignis in hesternō stīpite parvus erat

    hesternō diē is “yesterday” too (Cic. N. D. 2.73, Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • fuistī here nōbīscum

    you were with us yesterdaySen. Ep. 64.1

  • ignis in hesternō stīpite parvus erat

    a small fire was still burning in yesterday’s logOv. Fast. 5.506

See also today, the day before yesterday, yesterday morning, yesterday evening, last night.

SourcesLewis & Short: heri · Lewis & Short: hesternus
